disposition_reason: Primary flame AAS survey of Cd, Pb, Cu and Zn in 20 Egyptian market foods, dry-weight means.

study.design: Market survey of legumes, cereals, cereal products and packaged fried potatoes
study.market: various markets in East, West, Middle, Amriya and Montazah districts, Alexandria, Egypt
study.method: Oven drying (wet samples) and grinding, dry ashing at 550 C with HNO3 aid, flame AAS (air-acetylene, SOLAAR)
lod: Cd 0.002, Pb 0.001, Cu 0.001, Zn 0.002 ppm (in solution)
study.qa: Reagent blanks; spike recoveries Cd 87.44 ± 9.60, Pb 91.35 ± 8.73, Cu 100, Zn 95.21 ± 4.78%; no CRM

unresolved: Results are on a dry-weight basis; moisture not reported, so fresh-weight values cannot be derived.
Flame AAS detection limits printed (0.001-0.002 ppm in solution) are unusually low for flame AAS, especially for Pb.
Printed journal citation is Emir. J. Agric. Sci. 2005, 17(1): 34-42; the PDF prints no DOI and the manifest DOI encodes volume 12.
Brand names of the two fried potato products are replaced with brand A/B.

regulatory_or_exposure.value: Pb in cereals and legumes 0.2 mg/kg (CAC 2003); Cd all foods 0.05 mg/kg (Walker 1988); Cu 10 mg/kg (CAC 1993); Zn grains 50, beans 100 mg/kg (USDA 2003)

source_record_corrections: No DOI printed in the PDF; printed volume 17(1) vs manifest DOI suffix v12i1.
